questions.enonce_markdown: Given two statements $p$ and $q$. Draw a truth table for $\sim p\wedge\sim q$, using T for True and F for False. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Build the table column by column: first $p$ and $q$ (all four combinations), then $\sim p$ and $\sim q$ (the opposites), then the conjunction $\sim p\wedge\sim q$, which is true only when **both** $\sim p$ and $\sim q$ are true.

| $p$ | $q$ | $\sim p$ | $\sim q$ | $\sim p\wedge\sim q$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | F | F | F |
| T | F | F | T | F |
| F | T | T | F | F |
| F | F | T | T | T |

Row by row: (F and F) = F; (F and T) = F; (T and F) = F; (T and T) = T.

**Last column: F, F, F, T.** (It is true only when $p$ and $q$ are both false, so $\sim p\wedge\sim q$ is the same as $\sim(p\vee q)$.)
